steps.content: [Guest room]
Late at night, snow falls in silence.
You searched the entire manor but found no path down the mountain. Even more eerily, the manor master seems to have vanished without a trace.
The group turned the place upside down but found nothing, so they had no choice but to settle in the guest rooms for the night.
Schorl in your arms remains silent. The fire burns quietly in the brazier, casting light on Shuang'er as she sits hugging her knees.

You give the larger, softer bed to Shuang'er, but she simply stares wide-eyed toward the window in a daze. All the manor's guest rooms share the same layout, so the folding screen by the window is identical to the one in Jiewubei's room.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: I... I can't sleep. Every time I close my eyes, all I see is Master Wubei... cut up into pieces, laid out on the table like some kind of dish...
The scene was simply horrifying. Even you hadn't witnessed anything like it in DisCity, let alone an innocent girl like Shuang'er. You use the gauze curtains as a divider to shield her from the view.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Stop thinking about that. Come closer to the fire. Once you're warmed up, you'll be able to fall asleep. Maybe by dawn, the snow will have gotten lighter.
You carefully check the door bolt once more.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't worry, I'm keeping watch. No matter how elusive that manor master is, she won't be able to get in here.
Shuang'er seems to relax a little and obediently moves to lie down on the bed.

This bed is so much bigger and softer than the kang bed back in Ping'an Town. This room alone could shelter dozens of the town's children from the snow. Yet she's in no mood to enjoy such a "luxurious" place.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: Hey... this Northsnow Manor... is quite different from those famous places we've seen in martial world storybooks, right?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: How is it different?

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: In the storybooks, a master's retreat is usually a place where respectable elders greet guests amiably through ethereal mists and offer them martial arts teachings... A place where everyone drinks wine together under the moon, sharing tales of the martial world...
The fire crackles. Shuang'er curls up on the bed, wrapped in a thin blanket with only half her pale face visible.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: Earlier, at the foot of the mountain... I was telling tales of Guo Liqing crushing villains with his palm strikes, and of Qi Aofeng breaching fortresses with his sword. The children's eyes lit up as they listened. We all thought a visit to these famous places would be such a wonderful, awe-inspiring adventure.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: But now lying here, what keeps haunting my mind is Master Wubei's final moments... and those heroes' ice-cold stares.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I actually think the martial world here isn't so different from the one in your storybooks. There are heroes, martial arts, conflicts, and banquets in your tales. The same things are all present here.
Shuang'er pokes her head out, looking somewhat surprised.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's because in stories, we only keep the good parts. They glorify desire, hesitation, and the struggles of unfulfilled dreams, so people can focus on those honorable duels and heroic promises. After all, stories need to be satisfying and uplifting, right?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Even though certain parts of the stories are made up, the children still get all excited when they hear these tales. You... Ahem, we martial arts enthusiasts feel the urge to act virtuously ourselves after hearing such stories... All of that is real.
You add a piece of charcoal to the brazier, stirring up a few sparks.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If the blood-soaked martial world you saw today feels like this endless snowstorm, then think of the martial world you've always believed in as this fire.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: They both exist here.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: Are you saying we can still see the good side of the martial world?
She lifts her head, her eyes sparkling in the firelight.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes. Maybe... even better and more captivating than this fire! Something like... a delicious drumstick?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's not the whole reality, but it's definitely part of reality. As long as we believe it exists, we can always find it here.
Shuang'er nods, then, as if remembering something, pulls out several small medicine bottles from her pocket. She counts the pills one by one against the light, then swallows them all.

You know she isn't in good health, but this is the first time you've witnessed her downing all the pills. This martial hero gathering and the rumors about the codex might truly be the opportunity she's long hoped for to transform her physical condition.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Whatever can help you achieve your dream of becoming a great hero is definitely out there somewhere, waiting for you.
Shuang'er stares at you for a long moment, then purses her lips, though the corners of her mouth quietly curve into the faintest smile.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: You... can be such a fool sometimes.
She finally relaxes, stretching out her limbs and embracing the gradually warming candlelight.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: The snow keeps getting heavier... I wonder if we'll even be able to go down the mountain tomorrow. I miss Auntie Wang's beggar's chicken. You know, when you hold that dish, it warms your palms and feels so real. You can tell just from the smell that it'll fill your belly...
She turns over to face the wall, and soon her breathing becomes long and steady. In the dim light, her frame seems especially small and frail.
You blow out the candle. The room falls completely silent.

Those things you said to comfort Shuang'er aren't lies. If the power of heroes truly works like that of seers, that regardless of innate talent, they can gain power through being admired by people and accumulating good deeds, then it would be tremendously beneficial for Northwild, Eastia, and any place suffering from disasters.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But if there really is such a foolproof method of cultivation, then what would be the point of the Aurum Secretum smuggling that we've been investigating?

You clearly remember the terrifying power that manor master unleashed at the banquet. She receives no admiration or offerings from the people, nor has she done any widely celebrated heroic deeds. Where does her power come from then? What exactly is she trying to accomplish by creating this prison of snow?

The codex, the divine techniques... Your thoughts drift to these mysteries as you fall half asleep. From the small bed nearby comes Shuang'er's mumbled sleep talk, intermittent and mixed with some soft gulping noise.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: Drumstick... smells so good... Auntie Wang... I didn't steal the food... Who said they saw me do it?

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: No, it didn't happen if there's no witness... Ah, you might think... the smell comes from the stove, but what if...

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: ...The food has already been served at the table?
You suddenly snap awake and open your eyes in the darkness.

Since the start, no one has "seen" the manor master. That enticing "aroma," that "feast" hanging over everyone's heads, those manipulating hands waiting from behind the curtains... couldn't they actually have been present at the banquet?
[Somewhere in the Manor]
This night, no one at Northsnow Manor sleeps peacefully.
Shen Wanchou hasn't undressed at all. He paces back and forth restlessly beside the brocade-covered bed, his expensive cloud-patterned boots grinding messy tracks into the carpet.

The exquisitely carved glass lamp he brought sits on the desk, casting light on his brooding face. From time to time, he walks to the window and shoves the immovable frame, then glances with disgust at the brazier in the corner, provided by the manor and, in his view, utterly crude.

steps.speaker: Shen Wanchou
steps.content: What a heaven-forsaken place, and the snow never stops... Tch, they can't even afford to use silverbone charcoal? How stingy.
He yanks the bell-pull beside his bed to summon the servants, but gets no response. In his fury, he rips the decorative tassel off.

steps.speaker: Shen Wanchou
steps.content: Hmph, Manor Master Jiang, this treasure of yours better not be counterfeit. I would hate to have endured this awful blizzard for nothing.
[Somewhere in the Manor]

An eerie green light flickers in the darkness. Yin Yansheng sits cross-legged on a cushion. Before him spread his old turtle shell, which he always brings with him, and several polished ancient coins.
His gaunt fingers, dipped in a strange powder, draw twisted symbols on the floor. He mutters something under his breath while his cloudy eyes dart rapidly in their sunken sockets.

steps.speaker: Yin Yansheng
steps.content: An assault from the north while darkness lurks in the southeast... I see, this bloodshed is no new feud, but an old debt... Hehe, an old debt that was never fully repaid nor concealed, and now the snow has led it to us...
He suddenly snatches up the ancient coins, brings them close to his nose, and inhales deeply. His face shows both excitement and fear.

steps.speaker: Yin Yansheng
steps.content: This smell... I know it! Many years ago, in... in that graveyard. The same heavy snow, the same pungent stench of blood... No, no...

steps.speaker: Yin Yansheng
steps.content: Back! All back! This manor... it's waiting to claim us...
[Somewhere in the Manor]
A solitary lamp flickers in the wind. The snow bears two long wheel tracks, and at their end, Ji Guining sits alone in quiet contemplation.

Before her sits a messy mound of snow with a broken branch stuck into it, serving as makeshift incense. She presses her palms together, bows her head, and quietly recites prayers. Her expression is filled with sorrow, tears glistening at the corners of her eyes.

steps.speaker: Ji Guining
steps.content: Jiewubei, if your spirit harbors any unresolved grievances, speak to me. How did the manor master claim your life from such a distance? Tell me, and I shall avenge you.
[Somewhere in the Manor]
"Clang! Clang!"
The rhythmic, piercing sound of metal scraping cuts through the silence of the night.
Ma Ling takes a wide stance, the heavy black halberd laid flat on her knee. She holds a whetstone in her hand, running it along the halberd's blade again and again.
With each drag of the whetstone, the muscles in her shoulders and back tense, ready to unleash an explosive blow at any moment.

steps.speaker: Ma Ling
steps.content: Don't you want to take my life? Then don't lurk in the dark like a coward! Come out and face me in a proper fight!
[Somewhere in the Manor]
The feeble candle flame casts Xu Shen's frantic silhouette on the wall, his shadow shaky and twisted.

His face is deathly pale, cold sweat beading at his temples and nose. His breathing comes in short, rapid gasps. His hands move hurriedly and jerkily to stuff his clothes into his bag. As he packs, he strains to listen for any noise behind the door. The slightest sound can make him jump.

Something suddenly occurs to him, and he lunges toward the candlelight, pulling out a piece of paper. The paper is badly crumpled, with several lines written on it. A copy of that blood-stained denunciation. He reads the text once more.

steps.speaker: Xu Shen
steps.content: This place isn't safe... I can't wait until dawn... Now, I have to leave now...

He clutches his belongings tightly to his chest and curls up in the shadows behind the door. His eyes are fixed unblinkingly on the window as if vengeful spirits might emerge at any moment to claim his life.
[Somewhere in the Manor]

Unperturbed by the fearful atmosphere beneath her, Xiaofeng has fetched herself another jar of wine and half a cold roasted chicken. Ignoring the freezing cold, she sprawls comfortably in the snow on the rooftop, watching the manor's unfolding drama with keen interest, her hands greasy and her face flushed from her drink.
Once she has tossed the last bit of chicken bone into her mouth and crunched it loudly, she sighs contentedly, raising her wine jar in a toast to the invisible stage below.

steps.speaker: Mountain Lord
steps.content: Fine wine for a fine spectacle! Another cup!
Lights gradually go out throughout the manor. In the darkness, a spider slips into the chaos...
